- Use the Enterprise Wiki to create a single, go-to place for knowledge sharing and project management across the enterprise. Enterprise Wikis are simple to use, flexible, and lightweight in features. They are quick and easy to create, and you can easily add links to other information systems, corporate directories, or applications. By using an Enterprise Wiki, you can avoid email overload, provide structure to new and existing information, and encourage collaboration. This helps build consensus among team members. Working with content - text, graphics or video - is as easy as working in any word processing application, such as Microsoft Word. Use the Rich Text Editor to enhance the formatting of content, apply styles to text, reorganize or spell check your content, insert and format tables, and embed graphics or video. You can do all these things without leaving the wiki page. Other things you can do when working with Enterprise Wikis: Collaborate on wiki pages with other users Comment on a wiki page to enable discussion about the contents of the page Rate a wiki page to share your opinion about its content Categorize wiki pages to enable users to quickly find information and share it with others+ Information Resources Practice Areas and Working Groups Accounting Practice Area UK/EU Practice Group

- Courtroom View Network (CVN) Source Courtroom View Network (CVN) How to Cite the Source Courtroom View Network Description Courtroom View Network (CVN) delivers live and on-demand video and editorial coverage of high-stakes civil litigation. Since 2004, the CVN video library has grown to include over 1,000 trials with tens of thousands of hours of fully indexed, searchable video. Unless otherwise stated, all trials are fully indexed with evidence slides so that you see exactly what was presented at trial. Users can search by trial name, attorney, judge, expert witness, and more. Premium CVN docket, gavel-to-gavel CVN Video, and CVN Training services are provided as subscriptions, which provide access to trials, hearings, oral arguments, and other courtroom video that may be streamed over the Internet. Users may watch proceedings Live, or On Demand, on their personal computer, depending on the subscription. Video may also be viewed on DVD-ROM (Computer Only, playable in the CVN Player with synched digital exhibits) or DVD. When ordering DVDs, subscribers select proceedings at on CVN.com and receive them on DVD by U.S. mail or Fedex. CVN Video proceedings are designated into two categories: CVN Live Current Cases and CVN On Demand Archive Cases. CVN Live Current Cases are proceedings that are upcoming, in progress, or concluded within the last 30 days. These proceedings are available in one or all of the following formats: Live, On Demand, on DVD. A CVN Live subscription provides video access to all Current Cases, with premium events available only under a CVN Live Premium subscription. CVN On Demand Archive Cases are proceedings that concluded more than 30 days ago, and where the video has undergone a quality assessment, quality improvement where possible, and video chapters are logged for better browsing and navigation. These proceedings are available in these formats: DVD, On Demand. These proceedings are sold in a discount subscription and available through an annual CVN On Demand subscription. CVN's Editorial team finds trials using a variety of sources, including dockets and news articles. They also receive many tips and they poll subscribers to find out what they want to see. List of cases covered Time Period Covered 2004 - present Access Must purchase subscription Contact: #Information Resources Cost Video Library access online: https://cvn.com/pricing ($99 per month for 1 person, $399 per month for up to 6). This only includes online viewing of completed trials. Premium Live Access or Digital Downloads: Pricing for live and on-demand access to a single case is below. Each account or user would be able to log in from one device at a time. 1-3 accounts - $600 per day 4-6 accounts - $800 per day 7-9 accounts - $1000 per day Firm Wide - $1200 per day Downloadable files in addition to any option above would be $400 per day. Downloadable files would be delivered within 36 hours of each day ending. Live and on-demand access for the firm to all trials we cover would be $3,000 per month on an annual contract. Important Notes CVN focuses on civil litigation. Memberships automatically renew unless cancelled, which can be done on the Account page. Video Library memberships do not include access to live trials. CVN will periodically offer certain live trials to our members depending on interest. We would need to negotiate a license with CVN if we were to get a full subscription. AI Restrictions Parent company Remote Counsel (RC) grants users a limited license to access and make personal use of CVN and not to download (other than page caching) or modify it, or any portion of it, except with express written consent of RC. This license does not include any resale or commercial use of CVN.com or its contents; any collection and use of any product listings, descriptions, or prices; any derivative use of CVN.com or its contents; any downloading or copying of account information for the benefit of another merchant; or any use of data mining, robots, or similar data gathering and extraction tools. CVN.com and any portion of it content may not be reproduced, duplicated, copied, sold, resold, visited, or otherwise exploited for any commercial purpose without express written consent of RC. - EBSCO Source EBSCOHost How to Cite the - Source cite by publication Description EBSCO Has over 3,500 journals, magazines - and trade publications indexed and abstracted, 2,900 of them provide full - text. On the EBSCOHost main page, there are three searching interfaces to choose from: EBSCOHost This is the standard interface for EBSCO. Information Resources usually starts with the next option. Business Searching Interface The Business Searching Interface (BSI) is EBSCO's highly focused user interface created especially for the business searcher. The Business Searching Interface is a completely separate user experience from the typical EBSCOhost experience. This is IR's preferred interface Tutorial for Business Searching Interface Business Book Summaries Business Book Summaries® (BBS) provides comprehensive, yet concise summaries of the best business books available. Using stringent criteria, only the top 1% of the more than 6,000 business books published each year in the United States is selected for inclusion in the database. Summaries and reviews are provided for more than 700 of the top business books from the last 20 years. More information on BBS Cornerstone's EBSCO subscription includes the following databases: EconLit with Full Text EconLit with Full Text contains all of the indexing available in EconLit, plus full text for nearly 600 journals, including the American Economic Association journals with no embargo. This database also contains many non-English full-text journals in economics and finance. Volume and issue browsing is available for all full-text journals. EconLit adheres to the high quality standards long recognized by subscribers to the Journal of Economic Literature (JEL) and is a reliable source of citations and abstracts to economic research dating back to 1886. It provides links to full-text articles in all fields of economics, including capital markets, country studies, econometrics, economic forecasting, environmental economics, government regulations, labor economics, monetary theory, urban economics, and much more. EconLit uses the JEL classification system and controlled vocabulary of keywords to index six types of records: journal articles, books, collective volume articles, dissertations, working papers, and full-text book reviews from the Journal of Economic Literature. These sources bring the total records available in the database to more than 1.2 million. List of Full-Text Titles List of Titles by Subject Business Source Corporate Plus Business Source Corporate Plus  is designed to meet the diverse information needs of today's companies.  This product contains full text from more than 5,400 premium business magazines and journals.  BSC Plus also provides AP wires and thousands of newsfeeds, updated in real time. Additional sources include more than one million substantial company listings; over 2400 newspapers, 850,000 transcripts and more than 1,600 country economic reports. List of Magazines and Journals List of Other Sources List of Sources by Subject Newswires EBSCO's Newswires provides near real-time access to top world-wide news from Associated Press, United Press International, CNN Wire, and Business Wire on a continuous basis. This content is monitored by EBSCO and relevant results are provided when users enter searches in EBSCOhost. This collection includes AP Financial News, AP Top News, AP WorldStream, AP U.S. Politics & Government, AP 50 State Reports, UPI Business, UPI Entertainment, UPI Sports, UPI Top News, and more. End users can immediately access the full text of the web content, by following the link in the record. The index to the full text content in EBSCO Newswires is held for a rolling 30-day archive by EBSCO, so users can enjoy the previous 30 days of news relating to their search interests. Web News EBSCO's Web News provides near real-time access to thousands of top news feeds from around the globe. This collection includes over 14,000 feeds covering a range of business and general news topics. End users can immediately access the full text of the web content, by following the link in the record. EBSCO news source list.xlsx as of Dec 2021 See Cornerstone Comments below for more information on EBSCO's news coverage Business Book Summaries mentioned above Time Period + EBSCO Source EBSCOHost How to Cite the Source cite by publication Description EBSCO Has over 3,500 journals, magazines and trade publications indexed and abstracted, 2,900 of them provide full text. On the EBSCOHost main page, there are three searching interfaces to choose from: EBSCOHost This is the standard interface for EBSCO. Information Resources usually starts with the next option. Business Searching Interface The Business Searching Interface (BSI) is EBSCO's highly focused user interface created especially for the business searcher. The Business Searching Interface is a completely separate user experience from the typical EBSCOhost experience. This is IR's preferred interface Tutorial for Business Searching Interface Business Book Summaries Business Book Summaries® (BBS) provides comprehensive, yet concise summaries of the best business books available. Using stringent criteria, only the top 1% of the more than 6,000 business books published each year in the United States is selected for inclusion in the database. Summaries and reviews are provided for more than 700 of the top business books from the last 20 years. More information on BBS Cornerstone's EBSCO subscription includes the following databases: EconLit with Full Text EconLit with Full Text contains all of the indexing available in EconLit, plus full text for nearly 600 journals, including the American Economic Association journals with no embargo. This database also contains many non-English full-text journals in economics and finance. Volume and issue browsing is available for all full-text journals. EconLit adheres to the high quality standards long recognized by subscribers to the Journal of Economic Literature (JEL) and is a reliable source of citations and abstracts to economic research dating back to 1886. It provides links to full-text articles in all fields of economics, including capital markets, country studies, econometrics, economic forecasting, environmental economics, government regulations, labor economics, monetary theory, urban economics, and much more. EconLit uses the JEL classification system and controlled vocabulary of keywords to index six types of records: journal articles, books, collective volume articles, dissertations, working papers, and full-text book reviews from the Journal of Economic Literature. These sources bring the total records available in the database to more than 1.2 million. - Execucomp (Now Part Of S&P ) Source ExecuComp How to Cite the Source S&P ExecuComp Description S&P's executive compensation database can be used to identify company trends and industry peers. ExecuComp provides details on executive stock and option awards as well as pension plans to give you the full compensation picture. Selected company financials helps you compare executive pay to company performance. The ExecuComp database includes detailed breakouts of compensation data under the pre-2006 reporting rules so that you can research historical compensation trends. The ExecuComp database is released 6 times per year: January, March, April, May, June, and October. ExecuComp data is also available using the S&P Market Intelligence Professionals data set, which profiles professionals with current and prior board/company affiliations. Execucomp's data is a subset of the data available via the Professionals data feed.  The two databases have different naming conventions and organization, so mapping data variables between this is incredibly difficult. If you are replicating ExecuComp data, use the ExecuComp database, not Professionals.  Data includes biographies, standardized job functions, titles, education, compensation, options holdings, and full committee memberships. The People Basic SME data offering provides Professional data for private companies that do not file financials. The People Basic SME data is typically collected directly from the private company or through local company registries. The data points for People Basic SME include private company professionals metadata, inclusive of first and last name, gender year born, titles, unique person identifiers, job functions as reported, and flags indicating current or past board affiliations. Features: Covers more than 4.5 million professionals Compensation history going back to 1992 Over 40 different compensation types Gain insight on an individual's career history and professional relationships with current and prior information integrated into profiles of public and private company executives, board members, and investment professionals, globally Research individuals based on biography, contact data, education, compensation, affiliations, and corporate board membership information Make associations with a person's professional past, aligning a person's experience and relationships with your specific needs Focus on key decision makers, and not rank-and-file employees View committee membership details for board members and executives Evaluate the compensation of the chief executive officer (CEO) There is data on US and International companies (if the company files a proxy statement, there will be data.) Execucomp Professionals Database User Guide.pdf Execucomp Professionals Data Guide.xlsx exec_defs.doc Time Period Covered Compensation history back to 1992 Access Case teams must subscribe for access. Contact #Information Resources for more information Contact: Please contact #Information Resources for all inquiries Cost In 2024, the cost was $20,000 for 1 year of access for 3 users (we will need to get updated cost estimates for all new requests) Important Notes Delivery methods: XpressFeed (FTP File Transfer): This is our traditional data delivery method where your data team will install our proprietary software to receive the full dataset in a file via FTP (~30GB). This is the most common option used by our clients that are not using or interested in using Snowflake (cloud delivery). Whenever there are updates to the dataset (up to once per day), S&P will send you a "change file" with only the changes to the dataset where you will use that to update your dataset. Snowflake (Cloud Delivery): This option utilizes our partnership with Snowflake to deliver and store S&P data to you via cloud. With this option, you would incur the storage and compute costs necessary to power your queries, but clients usually find the pros of this delivery method outweigh the con of additional cost. For 30GB of data and relatively infrequent queries, I'd be surprised if you even paid $100 per year in snowflake fees. As I mentioned on our call, even if you don't have a current relationship with Snowflake, we can still leverage this delivery method through S&P paperwork through our partnership. With this option, you would access the data through a Snowflake portal (via web browser) and would require no "change files" to be managed by your team (we would handle that through Snowflake). You can read more about snowflake here: https://www.snowflake.com/en/why-snowflake/ We have access to some Execucomp data in Capital IQ. However, you need to pull the data by individual company.  It you want to pull large data pulls of executive data, you would need to subscribe to the product. Sales Navigator Account Types - Overview These account types all offer the following features: 100-mile maximum search radius from within a postal code 2,500 profiles shown per search Unlimited number of searches and up to 15 saved searches 15 saved search alerts per week Unlimited number of saved accounts Unlimited number of lead recommendations Access to the Sales Navigator app Access to Advanced search filters Sales Navigator Team With a Sales Navigator Team account, you'll have access to the following features: No limit to the number of Sales Navigator seats that can be purchased Sales Navigator Team free trials for up to 10 users. You can add these users at the beginning of your 30-day trial period, but adding any licenses after the initial order will result in a charge. - ​ Numerator Source Numerator How to Cite the Source Numerator Description Numerator is a data and technology company that provides a comprehensive, 360-degree view of consumer behavior by tracking the "what, where, and why" of every purchase. Unlike traditional market research firms that rely on fragmented store-level data, Numerator utilizes a massive, single-source "OmniPanel" of over 1 million U.S. households who share their buying habits directly via a receipt-scanning mobile app. This "zero-party" data approach allows the company to track more than 2 billion shopping trips across all retail channels, including e-commerce, warehouse clubs, and convenience stores—offering brands a "total commerce" perspective that legacy systems often miss. Time Period Covered Numerator's core purchase data from its OmniPanel tracks back to 2014 with a robust, comparable benchmark established in 2019 while its legacy archives for advertising and promotional data extend as far back as the 1990s Access Provide one-off requests, reach out to #Information Resources for access. Contact: Reach out to #Information Resources Cost $20,000-$100,000.  Please reach out to #Information Resources . Important Notes Only provide social media data for subscribers. See document for more information on media stations tracked: General Media Spend Tracking Universe (2).pdf Advertiser quick pivot tab can be provided to organize the data how you would like: Sample Offline Media Spend Numerator Report.xlsm Methodology in how they capture the ads. For digital specifically, they capture across about 10,000 sites. This document details the methodology and approach. Ad Intel Research Methodology Deck.pdf AI Restrictions Numerator strictly prohibits the use of automated bots or scraping tools to extract its data for training external AI models. To protect proprietary information, users are also restricted from uploading Numerator's reports into public AI platforms. Additionally, while their native AI tool, Nexa, provides deep insights, it is governed by rules that prevent the de-anonymization of consumers or the reverse-engineering of the company's technology. AI Definitions/Capabilities Beyond just tracking transactions, Numerator bridges the gap between consumer attitudes and actual behavior through its "Verified Voices" platform and advanced AI integrations. By connecting with verified buyers for on-demand surveys, the company helps brands understand the specific motivations behind a purchase and identify the "Say-Do" gap between what shoppers claim and what they actually buy. Recently, Numerator has further modernized its offerings with "Nexa," a conversational AI agent that allows users to ask complex business questions in natural language, enabling brands to instantly turn deep consumer insights into actionable growth strategies. - S&P DOW JONES INDICES Source https://www.spglobal.com/spdji/en/ How to Cite the Source © 20[xx] S&P Dow Jones Indices LLC Description Historical index constituents and total returns data Time Period Covered Varies by index Access Must purchase and license data directly from S&P Indices Exception: S&P Dow Jones Indices does not license intraday data. That data needs to be licensed directly from exchanges. A limited number of S&P indices are available from Tick Data. Intraday data may be available from CME and/or CBOE Contact: Please go through #Information Resources Cost As of 4/27/2026, $1,000 per year of data for one index, but we should ask for cost estimate for each request. In comparison, a subscription to access the data via LSEG Workspace would entail licensing the full index package that includes our requested index. For example, the DJ US index package is $30,000 per year and does not include history. Important Notes We cannot use data from the S&P Indices web site in our work. Most historical data for S&P indexes has to be licensed directly from S&P Indices. (There might be index price/value data in our other resources like Capital IQ and LSEG Workspace, but you're not likely to find constituents.) Purchasing and licensing data from S&P Indices can take a week, so please plan ahead. There are strict guidelines for licensing the data from S&P Indices, including: The index data must be subject to a Protective Order The amount of data used in the Expert Report must be limited. We can include only limited portions (both in terms of the amount of material obtained from the Services and the proportion of such amount as compared to the volume of content not from the Services within the Subscriber Expert Reports) of historical index values from the Services. S&P will need to verify the Permitted Data is publicly available prior to using it in a report When the matter has concluded, we must cease using the data. Constituent level data may not be reproduced. Opposing side will have to purchase data in order to replicate analysis Subscriber shall include in each Subscriber Expert Report, as it relates to the Permitted Data: (a) a notice indicating that the Permitted Data in the Subscriber Expert Report is only for use in connection with the relevant litigation and (b) the following legend, on behalf of S&P, its affiliates, and its third party licensors: "The [Insert name of applicable S&P index(es)] ("Index(es)") and associated data are a product of S&P Dow Jones Indices LLC, its affiliates and/or their licensors and has been licensed for use by [Subscriber].  © 20[xx] S&P Dow Jones Indices LLC, its affiliates and/or their licensors. - S3 Source S3 How to Cite the Source S3 Partners Description S3 Short Interest and Securities Finance data covers more than 60,000 global securities. The time series data includes financing rates (bid/ask/last), short interest, float data, open interest (long positions) and proprietary indexes (squeeze, crowded, momentum). Data points are broken up into four categories: Short Interest – Daily shorting activity for 60,000+ global securities Financing Rates – Unbiased bid, offer and last rates from all sides of the market Crowding – An indicator providing a measure of shorting and covering events relative to market float that predicts financing spikes in real-time Days-to-Cover – Number of days to close out all short positions Sample data: WF S3MomentumSqueeze 8-21-18to8-15-19.xlsx WF S3ShortInterest 8-21-18to8-15-19.xlsx WF S3Float 8-21-18to8-15-19.xlsx WF S3FinancingRates 8-21-18to8-15-19.xlsx Documentation: Data Overview - Short Interest v1.0.pdf Time Period Covered S3's data set and model are from 2015. S3 started distributing its data to clients in 2016. S3 does not save old versions of its model. Instead, it has point-in-time data (read more about this below). Access Two members of IR have access. Contact: #Information Resources Cost $1,000 per equity regardless of date range Important Notes S3 has $3T+ of assets under advisement and can live stream 5 million transactions across this asset base every day. As a result, S3 can provide a clear and comprehensive picture of the securities finance market in real time and fill the gap between regulatory publication dates with accurate short interest data. S3's goal is to provide the most comprehensive and accurate short interest data with the information available at the time S3 provide it. For this reason, when new short interest regulatory data is released, S3 revises its projections to reflect this new source of information. That said, S3 recognizes that its process for revising its projections can be problematic for clients who use S3 data to feed their internal models and conduct backtesting. For any client who needs it, S3 is able to provide a "point in time" data set that shows its data set as it appeared before it was updated to reflect new information from regulatory filings. Following are some notes from inquiries case teams have posed to S3: CR: When working with the S3 data, we learned that the data (both rates and short interest) is reported based on settled loans and therefore correspond to settlement dates not trade dates.  This means that for securities that settle on a T+2 or T+3 day cycle, if one wants to assess conditions an investor faced at the time of the trade, rate and short interest variables need to be shifted back by the appropriate number of days. Some questions we've asked S3 and their answers: CR: Do you know whether the "offer rate" reported by S3 Partners represents the average offer rate on a given day, or the last reported offer rate? S3: Offer Rate is not merely an average, but it is a "fair rate" that hedge funds should be paying for a particular stock borrow. It also takes into consideration the recent supply & demand characteristics for a particular security as well as directionality of recent rate flows. We are calculating what we believe to be the overall cost basis of stock borrow costs of a prime broker and adding on a "fair" profit spread for that security coupled with directionality and volatility of rate activity to come up with an offer rate that is both appropriate for the lender to charge and the borrower to pay. CR: For your measure of short interest, does that represent all short interest in the market, or only the short interest from certain types of market participants? S3: This includes any proprietary information we have on the short side which includes $3.5 trillion in assets along with the exchange reported numbers. This does not include all participants, for example if Goldman Sachs or any prime broker were to approve a short and they were utilizing their internal supply they would not have to publicly disclose this to the exchanges CR: For the last rate variable, can you confirm that the lending fee is an annual interest rate on the value of the stock borrowed? Or is it presented in some other unit? S3: The attached data dictionary will give you the definition of each of our rate fields, (bid, offer and last), the bid rate on any given day is the amount you would earn on that day (quantity* closing price/360) is the dollar amount you would earn on that day. Assuming the rate didn't move the entire year that would be the annualized number you would earn. CR: I see in some instances that the "SI Pct S3 Float" variable is greater than 100%.  I understand how this number can be over 100% if the float is only considering actual shares outstanding.  But if the S3 Float "includes synthetic longs created by short selling", can that number still be greater than 100%?  Or would that potentially be a result of some missing/inconsistent information between the two variables, such as the example you give with Goldman utilizing their internal supply? S3: When calculating short interest, the formula is number of shares short divided by the float. That said there is no limit as to how many times a broker can re-hypothecate your shares. Look at GME in January of 2021 and you will notice that traditional SI% was hovering at 140%, so we take our short interest projection in shares and add this back into the denominator to get a better understanding of the true capacity in the marketplace. To highlight this, let's assume GME had 1,000 shares as its entire float and you're long those shares, I subsequently short those shares and my broker borrows them from you, I in-turn short those shares and it ends up in someone else's account. We have effectively increased the number of long holders to two people with an aggregate of 2,000 share. There is nothing holding the broker back from re-hypothecating those shares. This has nothing to do with internalization but just the mechanics of the marketplace. That's why we came up with the S3% float to account for these situations and effectively adding the number of shares short back into the denominator. CR: It looks like the price variable in the data we pulled is lagged by a day, such that the price in the S3 data on Tuesday is the closing price we see on Monday from other data sources.  I did not see any price variable in the data dictionary you shared, so I was hoping you could confirm whether this variable is meant to represent the prior day's closing price, or if there was an issue with the price/date in the data we pulled. S3: Correct the prices in our data set reflect the previous days close. For context, in the securities lending market the rate you're going to pay is based on a stock's closing price. CR: We understand that the variable "SI %" is calculated as "SI Shares" divided by an estimate of float.  (Our data dictionary refers to it as "S3 float." S3: We take the number of shares short for that day and add them back into the denominator or float to get the S3 Float CR: Could you provide details on how float is calculated or if provided by a third-party vendor, who is the vendor? S3: The float number comes from FactSet CR: You mentioned that there is a variable "Utilization" that can be used as a proxy for supply.  However, we do not see this variable in our data. Could you check if this field is available and if included in our contract? S3: Checking to see if utilization is available CR: Could you provide details on how utilization is calculated and what underlying data source is used? S3: Provided in data dictionary. We are consuming availability files from prime brokers on a daily basis to get an estimate of lendable quantity CR: We understand that data associated with a date X is based on trades that settled on or before that date X (and thus would have been executed prior to date X). Could you confirm that this understanding is correct? S3: The short interest for that day example 6/22, represents all settled trades for 6/22. On a T+2 settlement cycle these trades these trades would have been executed on the 20th CR: Could you confirm that this is applicable to the interpretation of "Bid," "Offer," "Last," "SI Share," as well as to variables derived from "SI Share" ("SI %" or "Utilization")? S3: Bid and offer represent the weighted average of where the market is through that settlement date and are updated at 8am the following day. The last rate is the last print for that day. CR: For example, if one is trying to assess the offer or bid rates associated with short transactions executed on or before a date X, assuming a T+2 settlement cycle, the corresponding data would be "Bid" and "Offer" on date X+2 (based on trading days). S3: Referring to my example above 6/22 would be the weighted bid/offer for all trades settled through 6/22. In theory these would be the rates offered on TD ^/20 CR: Similarly, if one is trying to match short positions that were executed on or before a date X (and settled after date X) with Bloomberg closing prices on date X, assuming T+2 settlement cycle, the corresponding data would be "SI Shares" or "SI %" on date X+2 (based on trading days) S3: Are short interest projections on 6/22, along with bid/offer rates are through that settle date, 6/22 and the rate you would pay on the financing would correspond to 6/22 closing prices on Bloomberg. In theory these trades would be executed on TD 6/20. AI Restrictions Would need to contact S3 AI Definitions/Capabilities S3 does not appear to have any AI-related offerings Updated 5/22/2026_hg+ S3 Source S3 How to Cite the Source S3 Partners Description S3 Short Interest and Securities Finance data covers more than 60,000 global securities. The time series data includes financing rates (bid/ask/last), short interest, float data, open interest (long positions) and proprietary indexes (squeeze, crowded, momentum). Data points are broken up into four categories: Short Interest – Daily shorting activity for 60,000+ global securities Financing Rates – Unbiased bid, offer and last rates from all sides of the market Crowding – An indicator providing a measure of shorting and covering events relative to market float that predicts financing spikes in real-time Days-to-Cover – Number of days to close out all short positions Sample data: WF S3MomentumSqueeze 8-21-18to8-15-19.xlsx WF S3ShortInterest 8-21-18to8-15-19.xlsx WF S3Float 8-21-18to8-15-19.xlsx WF S3FinancingRates 8-21-18to8-15-19.xlsx Documentation: Data Overview - Short Interest v1.0.pdf Time Period Covered S3's data set and model are from 2015. S3 started distributing its data to clients in 2016. S3 does not save old versions of its model. Instead, it has point-in-time data (read more about this below). Access Two members of IR have access. Contact: #Information Resources Cost $1,000 per equity regardless of date range Important Notes S3 has $3T+ of assets under advisement and can live stream 5 million transactions across this asset base every day. As a result, S3 can provide a clear and comprehensive picture of the securities finance market in real time and fill the gap between regulatory publication dates with accurate short interest data. S3's goal is to provide the most comprehensive and accurate short interest data with the information available at the time S3 provide it. For this reason, when new short interest regulatory data is released, S3 revises its projections to reflect this new source of information. That said, S3 recognizes that its process for revising its projections can be problematic for clients who use S3 data to feed their internal models and conduct backtesting. For any client who needs it, S3 is able to provide a "point in time" data set that shows its data set as it appeared before it was updated to reflect new information from regulatory filings. S3: A date of Sep 18 indicates the date it was published, which reflects all settled positions through the prior business date (Sep 17) and trades executed on Sep 16 (assuming t+1 markets).  So, the Date field represents the publish/business date of the S3 file, rather than the date on which the underlying positions were established. A file dated September 18 is published on September 18, but the short interest values reflect positions as of the prior business day's close (September 17). In T+1 settlement markets, those positions would incorporate trades executed on September 16 that settled on September 17. This convention is used consistently across regions and historical files, with the Business Date corresponding to the SOD publication date. In your Memorial Day example: 5/29/2023 (Memorial Day) reflects the prior business day's settled positions (5/26). 5/30/2023 would also reflect the same underlying settled positions because no market activity occurred on the holiday and there were no new positions settled on 5/29. As a result, it is expected that the short interest values for 5/29 and 5/30 are identical. The first meaningful change would generally appear in the subsequent file on 5/31 once new trades have had an opportunity to settle and flow into the model. - CRIKIT Every Individual in Every Role Is Essential to and Entrusted with the Success of Cornerstone Research. CRIKIT is the Cornerstone Research resource for the development and preservation of intellectual capital.   All employees are invited to use and contribute to this firm wide resource. Some material may be inappropriate for a public content management system.   We expect contributions to be consistent with our core values, emphasize respect, and exhibit high quality. Content should be peer reviewed whenever practical before publishing to CRIKIT.  Content is intended for internal use only and should not be copied, printed, or used for external purposes without the approval of the content manager or content author.  Copyright requirements and court, client, and Cornerstone Research imposed requirements with respect to confidentiality must be followed. Cornerstone Research expressly disclaims any implied warranty or representation about the information or accuracy, relevance, timeliness, completeness, or appropriateness for any particular purpose of any kind presented on CRIKIT. The information presented on CRIKIT is submitted by third parties, is provided only as courtesy, reference and/or resource and does not imply, directly or indirectly, Cornerstone Research's endorsement, sponsorship or approval of the information, nor does any of the information reflect the opinions, analyses, positions, standards or policies of Cornerstone Research, any of its employees, or any expert supported by Cornerstone Research.+ Information Resources Practice Areas and Working Groups Accounting Practice Area UK/EU Practice Group

- Wall Street Journal Source Wall Street Journal How to Cite the Source Wall Street Journal, Dow Jones & Co. Description The Wall Street Journal is an American newspaper based in New York City. The newspaper provides extensive coverage of news, especially business and finance. Time Period Covered Most current three months Access Cornerstone has WSJ Group Access.  It means you will be able to easily access the WSJ from anywhere without being logged into Cornerstone's network after your initial set up. Follow these instructions . If you have any issues logging in, please follow the instructions below: Clear cookies by entering www.wsj.com/delete_cookies on the browser's address bar. Log out from the WSJ account by entering www.wsj.com/logout on the browser's address bar. Then try logging in again with your credentials. Cornerstone also has access to all verticals of WSJ Pro, which are Central Banking, Private Equity, Venture Capital, Bankruptcy, Cybersecurity and Artificial Intelligence. ​This is a completely different subscription than the one we have for the Wall Street Journal. To learn more about WSJ Pro visit our page HERE . Contact: Cost No Cost Important Notes For articles older than three months, please email #Information Resources with requests. Setting up WSJ alerts Once you are logged into the WSJ Online using the hyperlink in the above "Access" section, you can scroll down to the end of the WSJ Homepage and find the link for "Alerts" under the heading "Tools & Formats".  Alerts can be set using keywords or ticker symbols (this works for US securities only) Alerts can be delivered in real time or set to deliver once a day at a specified time.  Alerts can only be delivered to one email address.  All alerts will share this single email address.  (i.e. If you are setting different alerts with the intention of delivering them to different colleagues, you will have to send them to yourself first and forward them on individually.) Just a reminder that content from these subscriptions are for individual use and/or research purposes only. Please contact #Information Resources if you want to produce articles for a case or share externally and we'll try to get a shareable copy for you. AI Restrictions AI Definitions/Capabilities Dow Jones & Company Artificial Intelligence Terms of Use. It is the most-widely circulated newspaper within the Washington metropolitan area and has a large national audience. Daily broadsheet editions are printed for D.C., Maryland, and Virginia. Time Period Covered Access Firmwide Access, Contact  #InformationResources Contact Cost Free Important Notes Just a reminder that content from these subscriptions are for individual use and/or research purposes only Please contact #Information Resources if you want to produce articles or share externally and we'll try to get a shareable copy for you. AI Restrictions AI Definitions/Capabilities "Ask The Post AI": The Post launched an independent AI answer engine that is trained on its own news and journalism. This tool is designed to provide readers with streamlined information from the paper's extensive archives by allowing them to ask questions in a conversational format. The tool's responses are based exclusively on The Post's published reporting. The experimental tool leverages news articles published by The Washington Post's award-winning newsroom since 2016, ranking the results based on relevancy. To uphold the integrity of the reporting, a threshold for scoring relevant reporting for any given question has been set (i.e. if the tool doesn't readily find a relevant article – even if one is published – an answer won't be served). The tool's responses are based exclusively on The Post's published reporting. The experimental tool leverages news articles published by The Washington Post's award-winning newsroom since 2016, ranking the results based on relevancy. - ​FAQ 1.  Copyright Restrictions 2.  How CRIKIT got it's name 3. Taxonomy 1.  Copyright Restrictions To comply with copyright restrictions, the following policies apply on CRIKIT: For Crikit Materials Any materials found on Crikit cannot be included verbatim into any work product. For Academic Literature In general all Academic papers should be added to the Academic Literature section of CRIKIT in the appropriate JEL category using the Academic Paper Template Please provide the link to the source - JSTOR, EBSCO (both available via Library Page on the Portal), SSRN, etc. Once the paper has been added under Academic Literature, you may link to that page from anywhere else in CRIKIT (for example, cite to it (see example)). In the rare instances where you feel the need to upload the paper directly to CRIKIT, please contact the IR  regarding the copyright policies for the paper in question. Please do not upload the paper unless you received an explicit permission from the IR. For Court Opinions If the Court opinion is obtained from the Court's website, you may upload it to CRIKIT directly.  Please provide the link the source (court's page) as appropriate. We cannot upload anything downloaded from Lexis or Westlaw. For Government Reports Please provide a link to the source directly (i.e. FCC page with the report in question) instead of uploading the report to CRIKIT. For additional information about Copyright, go here . 2.  How CRIKIT got it's name Background note: "wiki" in "Wikipedia" comes from "wiki wiki" which means "quick" in Hawaiian. An e-mail solicitation of possible names for Cornerstone Research (CR) knowledge management and sharing system among analysts and associates produced a list of suggestions.  A shortlist was offered to the members of Knowledge Sharing Task Force and by popular vote the name Crikit was chosen. "CRIKIT" comes from CR+WIKI+IT as in "Find it!" (and make it snappy - "wiki"). It is pronounced like "cricket." Thanks to Matt Lambert (formerly CRSF) for suggesting the winning entry. 3. - ​(20090204) Out with the old and in with the new.  Announcing the new IR Wiki/Portal Site From: Londa, Laura To: #Cornerstone Research < CornerstoneResearch@cornerstone.com > Hello everyone, As a result of suggestions from you all and our own desire to more easily update our information for your use, we have merged our portal page with our new Crikit site ( http://crikit/Information_Resources ).  If you go to the Information Resources Community on the portal, you will now see our Crikit site embedded there.  With Crikit, we were able to create a site that was more dynamic and able to handle many more types and forms of information. However we did not want to entirely abandon the portal as we know many people turn to it first, and we found that certain portal-specific applications could not be brought over.  Thus to access CRSP or to add yourself to one of our TOC Routing lists, you will still need to go to the portal. However I think you will really like some of the new things we have added to our new site. A few of the more interesting things you will find are Updated pricing list for the data we download Complete copies of the Institutional Investor's All-American Research Team articles from 1990 to present and broken out by year and by industry! Detailed information on all of the outside data sources that Cornerstone uses (including costs and how to source them). (Please feel free to add your own comments on the source as well or add new sources to the list.) FAQ with answers to commonly asked IR questions like time stamps, NAICS and SIC codes, Factiva Sources, etc. Searching tips and tricks for the databases you have access to And much, much more! And if you think there is something missing, don't hesitate to let us know.  We can easily add and update everything.  With this new site, we will be continuing to add new information and resources for you.  At the top of the main page you will see the latest announcements regarding changes to the page or to our resources.  So come on in and look around and let us know what you think.  ( http://crikit/Information_Resources ). Long Live Crikit! --Information Resources Laura L. Londa Director of Information Resources Cornerstone Research 353 Sacramento Street, 23rd Floor San Francisco, CA  94111 Direct Dial:  415-229-8153 Fax:  415-229-8199 Email: llonda@cornerstone.com http://www.cornerstone.com

+ CRSP Indices​ From: Tam, Eric (1/28/2011) To: Gigante, Peter < pgigante@cornerstone.com >; #CRSP Support < CRSPSupport@cornerstone.com > CC: O'Mahony, Leslie < lomahony@cornerstone.com >; Maracaba, Wladimir < WMaracaba@cornerstone.com >; #Information Resources < InformationResources@cornerstone.com > Hi everyone, CRSP changed their U.S. Stock Database product in 2009 so that we no longer receive the NYSE/Amex/Nasdaq index.  Instead, we get the NYSE/Amex/Nasdaq/Arca index.  The old index may still exist in their other products, but we don't get it anymore.  If you really want it, I'm sure you can buy it from them separately. + ​How do I create a link to a file or document residing on the LAN? From: Czegledi, Katalin (3/24/2009) To: #Library < Library@cornerstone.com > Hi all - The easy way didn't work for me but the alternative way did. kc A. An easy way: Open the page for editing Open Microsoft Outlook and create a new Mail Message (which you would not be sending, so no addressees are needed) Cut and paste your link to the LAN folder or the document in the new Outlook message, i.e. <link> For example < \\crwadmin1\consulting\somefilename.doc > Copy the link from your Outlook message into your page Alter the text of the link if you would like to display a simple text rather than the path to the folder or the document For example replace < \\crwadmin1\consulting\somefilename.doc > with Important Document Save the page B. An alternative way: Open the page for editing Type the link title, select it, and click Insert Link (click the right mouse button ot the chain link icon on the editor's bar) You need the "Link to" part of the Search tab in Make link dialog. Next you have a choice. You can either (a) in the "Link To" portion of the Search Tab type your link in the format file://link/ For example, if linking \\crwadmin1\consulting\somefilename.doc then type: file://crwadmin1/consulting/somefilename.doc Please note: you must replace backslashes (\) with forward slashes (/) or (b) In the "Link To" portion of the Search tab type file:/// wait for a file icon to appear at the right of the "Link to" line, then click on the icon and navigate the LAN to your document or folder next, in the "Link to" part of the Search tab , replace backslashes (\) with forward slashes (/) Verify that the link in the "Link To" part of the Search tab looks like this: file://crwadmin1/consulting/somefilename.doc 5.  Save the Page http://portal.cornerstone.com/portal/server.pt/community/information_resources/293- ​How do I create a link to a file or document residing on the LAN? From: Czegledi, Katalin - (3/24/2009) To: #Library < Library@cornerstone.com > Hi all - The easy way didn't work for me but the - alternative way did. kc A. An easy - way: Open the page for editing Open Microsoft Outlook and create a new Mail - Message (which you would not be sending, so no addressees are needed) Cut and paste your link to the LAN folder or - the document in the new Outlook message, i.e. <link> For example - < \\crwadmin1\consulting\somefilename.doc > Copy the link from your Outlook message into your page Alter the text of the link if you would - like to display a simple text rather than the path to the folder or the document For example replace - < \\crwadmin1\consulting\somefilename.doc > with Important Document Save the page B. An alternative way: Open the page for editing Type the link title, select it, and - click Insert Link (click the right mouse button ot the chain - link icon on the editor's bar) You need the "Link to" part of the Search - tab in Make link dialog. Next you have a - choice. You can either - (a) in the "Link To" portion of the Search Tab type your link in the format file://link/ For example, if - linking \\crwadmin1\consulting\somefilename.doc then type: file://crwadmin1/consulting/somefilename.doc Please note: you must - replace backslashes (\) with forward slashes (/) or (b) In the "Link - To" portion of the Search tab type file:/// wait for a file icon to appear at the right of - the "Link to" line, then click on the icon and navigate the LAN to your - document or folder next, in the "Link to" part of the Search - tab , replace backslashes (\) with - forward slashes (/) Verify that the - link in the "Link To" part of the - Search tab looks like this: file://crwadmin1/consulting/somefilename.doc 5.  Save the Page http://portal.cornerstone.com/portal/server.pt/community/information_resources/293
